name: ToolLLM / ToolBench - Facilitating LLMs to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs (ToolLLaMA + API Retriever + DFSDT + ToolEval)
venue: ICLR 2024 (spotlight). Preprint arXiv:2307.16789 (cs.AI; cs.CL; cs.LG), v1 submitted 31 Jul 2023, v2 revised 3 Oct 2023; published at the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2024 (OpenReview id dHng2O0Jjr).

code_url: https://github.com/OpenBMB/ToolBench (official; codes, ToolLLaMA models, API retriever, ToolBench data and ToolEval). Models on HuggingFace (ToolBench/ToolLLaMA-2-7b-v2 etc.).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/OpenBMB/ToolBench (actively maintained; ICLR'24 spotlight). Successor/stabilized evaluation: StableToolBench (https://github.com/THUNLP-MT/StableToolBench) which adds an API simulator/caching to address RapidAPI temporal instability.
task_domain: tool-use (LLM tool learning): instructing LLMs to call external real-world RESTful APIs to fulfill natural-language instructions, including single-tool and multi-tool, multi-step solution paths. Also touches planning/decision-making (DFSDT tree search) and retrieval (API retriever) over a 16k+ API pool.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent tool use. Given a user instruction and a (large) pool of RapidAPI tools/APIs, an LLM must select and call APIs over multiple turns to produce a solution path (chain of API calls). Two operational settings: (a) ORACLE setting where the ground-truth relevant API subset is given to the model (simulating a user who specifies preferred APIs); (b) RETRIEVER setting where, from the full 16,464-API pool, a trained neural API retriever supplies top-5 candidate APIs (practical setting; no manual API recommendation). Supervision: instruction-tuning data (ToolBench) is auto-generated by ChatGPT (instructions + DFSDT-annotated solution paths); ToolLLaMA is obtained by SFT on LLaMA. The retriever is trained with contrastive learning on instruction->relevant-API pairs. Evaluation is reference-free via ChatGPT-based ToolEval (pass rate, win rate) because ground-truth solution paths are not fixable (RapidAPI APIs change over time; infinitely many valid paths). Generalization is tested to unseen instructions, unseen tools, and unseen categories.
what_is_retrieved: tools / APIs (real-world RESTful API endpoints from RapidAPI Hub), represented by their API documents. The neural API retriever recommends a small set (top-5) of relevant APIs for an instruction from the 16,464-API pool.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed pool of 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs (with documentation) crawled from RapidAPI Hub, spanning 49 categories. The retrievable store is frozen (constructed offline); the agent does not write new tools/experiences back into it. (Note RapidAPI itself is live/temporally variable, which motivates ToolEval's reference-free evaluation, but the indexed API corpus used for retrieval/training is a static snapshot.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective. The API retriever returns the top-5 APIs and is evaluated as a ranking task with NDCG@1 and NDCG@5. For multi-tool instructions (I2/I3) the relevant set has multiple APIs, so recovering the needed API set matters, but it is operationalized as a ranking metric (NDCG) and a fixed k=5 candidate feed to ToolLLaMA, not a variable-size precision-driven recommendation nor an explicit minimal-set-completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). Loose mapping: Retrieve = yes (API retriever); Reuse = partial (retrieved APIs are used as the candidate action space for the solver, not retrieval of prior solution cases); Revise = no; Retain = no. So effectively only a Retrieve phase over tools, not a case-based reasoning cycle.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as tool learning / instruction tuning for tool use + API retrieval + tree-search reasoning.
retrieval_unit: tool-API: a single real-world RESTful API endpoint, indexed via its API document (tool name, API name, description, parameters/category). Granularity is the API/function level (each API is a retrievable item; a 'tool' on RapidAPI may expose multiple APIs).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-constructed. 16,464 RESTful APIs (and their documents) crawled from RapidAPI Hub across 49 categories (filtered from a larger initial crawl, retaining APIs that respond reliably). The retriever's training labels (positive APIs per instruction) come from the ChatGPT-generated ToolBench instructions. No online/test-time growth of the index.
index_structure_topology: Underlying RapidAPI has a natural hierarchy (category -> collection -> tool -> API) which ToolBench exploits for instruction generation (intra-category I2, intra-collection I3) and generalization splits. The retriever itself, however, uses a FLAT dense vector index: each API document is encoded into an embedding and ranked by cosine similarity to the instruction embedding (no graph/dependency structure in the retriever). So: hierarchical metadata over tools used for data construction; flat embedding index used for retrieval.
retriever_type: Dense retriever (bi-encoder). Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) initialized from BERT-BASE (Devlin et al. 2019), encoding instruction and API document into embeddings and scoring by embedding similarity. Compared against BM25 (sparse) and OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 (off-the-shelf dense) baselines.
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive learning on similarity labels. For each instruction, the relevant APIs (from the ChatGPT-generated ToolBench instruction-API pairs) are positives and a few other sampled APIs are negatives; the Sentence-BERT bi-encoder is trained to pull instruction and relevant-API embeddings together. This is supervised-contrastive (relevance-label) training, not LM-feedback, RL, or downstream-task-effectiveness signal.
query_construction: Raw user instruction used directly as the query, encoded by the trained retriever and matched against API-document embeddings. No query decomposition, synthetic expansion, or intent extraction; no thought-conditioning.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is issued per instruction to obtain the top-5 candidate APIs, which then form the action space for the entire DFSDT solving process. Retrieval is not re-issued per reasoning step.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot. The API retriever is invoked once per instruction (returning top-5 APIs) before/at the start of solving. The subsequent multi-step solving (DFSDT) operates over this fixed candidate set; APIs are selected/called per step from the retrieved set but no new retrieval is triggered mid-trajectory.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: always retrieve once per instruction (in the retriever setting) before solving. There is no confidence/uncertainty/reflection-token trigger and no learned router deciding when to retrieve.
reranking: No explicit second-stage reranker. The dense retriever produces the ranked top-5 directly via embedding similarity. (DFSDT can be seen as a downstream selection/search over the retrieved/oracle APIs, but it is a solver, not a retrieval reranker.)
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond top-5 truncation. The top-5 retrieved API documents are passed to ToolLLaMA as the available tool set; there is no decompose-recompose, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering of the retrieved API documents.
tool_document_engineering: API documents are used largely as structured RapidAPI metadata (tool name, API name, description, required/optional parameters, category, example responses). For solving, the prompt presents the available APIs' documentation (a system prompt of API definitions). No synthetic-query augmentation, expanded-summary generation, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings beyond the contrastive Sentence-BERT training; the retriever embeds the API document text.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit. The retriever first narrows 16,464 APIs to a top-5 candidate set, and only those API documents are loaded into the solver's prompt (lightweight retrieval over the full pool, then heavier per-API documentation injected only for selected candidates). There is no formal progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content protocol; it is a standard retrieve-then-feed-top-k pattern.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Integration protocol = RapidAPI: APIs are real RESTful endpoints called live via RapidAPI during solution-path execution. The retrievable API index is a STATIC crawled snapshot (16,464 APIs), not live-synchronized with CRUD auto-sync. Not function-calling-schema or MCP based; tool calls are emitted in the ReAct/DFSDT format and executed against RapidAPI. (RapidAPI's runtime temporal variability motivated the later StableToolBench API simulator/cache.)
tool_dependency_awareness: No explicit inter-tool dependency modeling in the retriever. Multi-tool instructions (I2 intra-category, I3 intra-collection) involve composing multiple APIs, and DFSDT chains API calls (output of one call can inform the next) during solving, but the retriever ranks APIs independently by instruction similarity and does not model output-of-A-feeds-B dependencies, shared auth, or prerequisites via a dependency graph.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation defining the action space. Retrieved (top-5) or oracle API documents are placed in the solver prompt as the set of callable tools; ToolLLaMA then plans and emits API calls over these tools, executes them against RapidAPI, and reasons over returned responses to produce a final answer. Retrieval thus supplies the candidate toolset; it is not used as a training signal or latent-token injection at inference.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan/act, with planning realized by a depth-first search-based decision tree (DFSDT). After one-shot retrieval supplies the candidate APIs, the LLM performs DFSDT: it expands a tree of reasoning/action nodes (each node = a thought + an API call + observation), can evaluate multiple traces, backtrack from dead-ends/failed calls, and expand the search space beyond a single ReAct chain. Retrieval is one-shot at plan time; the search/tree exploration is internal to the solver over the fixed retrieved toolset.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a rollout. Within DFSDT, reasoning (thought) and acting (API call) alternate per node/step, and the tree explores multiple such per-step branches with backtracking. Retrieval itself is per-answer (one retrieval per instruction), but tool-use reasoning is interleaved per API call inside the tree search.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw API documentation (structured text: tool/API name, description, parameters, category) injected verbatim into the solver prompt as the available tools. Not a distilled strategy, workflow, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool/API specification (a reusable callable action with its documentation), i.e., the action/affordance level. Not a raw trajectory, demonstration, distilled strategy, or workflow; it is the executable tool interface to be invoked.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited / implicit. ToolLLaMA is instruction-tuned on DFSDT-annotated trajectories that include handling failed API calls (errors, invalid responses), and DFSDT's backtracking lets the solver recover from dead-ends and irrelevant/non-functional APIs. Empirically, feeding retriever top-5 (which may include APIs not in the oracle set) slightly OUTPERFORMS the oracle set, indicating robustness to and even benefit from broadened candidates. There is no explicit retriever-aware distractor-filtering, relevance evaluator, or self-reflection module dedicated to retrieved-context noise.
memory_type: none (no persistent agent memory). The system uses a static external API corpus for retrieval and the in-context DFSDT search tree as transient working state; nothing is stored across tasks/episodes. No episodic, skill-library, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: False. No experiences/cases/skills/tools are written back into a memory or the index during deployment. (Offline, ChatGPT-generated solution paths form the SFT training data, but this is dataset construction, not runtime write-back.)
online_growth: False. The API index and the model are frozen after construction/training; the retrievable store does not grow at test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back mechanism). During offline DATA construction, only successfully-passed DFSDT solution paths are RETAINED as training data (a success-filtered dataset-building step), but this is not runtime memory write-back.
failure_experience_usage: Success-filtered for training data (only passed/valid DFSDT solution paths are kept as ToolLLaMA training trajectories; failed search branches are discarded rather than stored as negative experiences for retrieval). At inference, DFSDT uses failed/invalid API responses transiently to backtrack within the current tree, but failures are not persisted or contrastively retrieved. No failure-memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no memory store to evolve). The API index is static; no dedup-merge/delta-update/refine/prune at runtime.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: the API retriever is a TRAINED (contrastive Sentence-BERT) model, so retrieval is learned rather than off-the-shelf, but it is a fixed similarity-based top-k retriever, NOT an RL/value-based or interactively-optimized retrieval policy. Selection is supervised on relevance labels, not optimized via downstream task reward.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent; no cross-agent/cross-framework memory sharing. The ToolBench dataset, API retriever, and ToolEval are shared community resources reused by later work, but at runtime there is no shared memory among multiple agents.
benchmarks: ToolBench (introduced here): test sets across three scenarios and three generalization levels, instantiated as six test subsets - I1 (single-tool): I1-Instruction, I1-Tool, I1-Category; I2 (intra-category multi-tool): I2-Instruction, I2-Category; I3 (intra-collection multi-tool): I3-Instruction. (Repo labels these G1/G2/G3 x {Instruction, Tool, Category}; ~200 sampled test instructions per subset.) Also: APIBench (Gorilla; TorchHub, TensorHub, HuggingFace) for OOD generalization. Underlying corpus: 16,464 RapidAPI RESTful APIs across 49 categories.
benchmark_family: tool (ToolBench/RapidAPI) - the canonical real-world API tool-use benchmark; plus tool (APIBench/Gorilla, ML model-hub APIs) for OOD. ToolBench is the origin of the 'ToolBench' family (later stabilized as StableToolBench) referenced throughout tool-retrieval/tool-use literature.
baselines: Reasoning strategies: ReAct, ReACT@N (cost-matched repeated ReAct), vs DFSDT. Models (each with ReAct and/or DFSDT): ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo, teacher), Text-Davinci-003, GPT-4, Claude-2, Vicuna, Alpaca, and ToolLLaMA (fine-tuned LLaMA). API-retriever baselines: BM25 and OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 vs the trained Sentence-BERT retriever. OOD baseline: Gorilla (LLaMA-7B fine-tuned on APIBench) in zero-shot (ZS) and retrieval-aware (RS) settings.
key_metrics: Tool use (ToolEval, ChatGPT-based): Pass Rate (proportion of instructions completed within a limited budget; executability) and Win Rate (ChatGPT preference vs the reference ChatGPT-ReACT solution; >50% means better than ChatGPT-ReACT). API retrieval: NDCG@1 and NDCG@5. OOD (APIBench): hallucination rate and AST accuracy. ToolEval human-agreement: 87.1% (pass rate), 80.3% (win rate).
headline_result: ToolLLaMA matches ChatGPT and, with its trained API retriever, performs best among the open framework variants. In ToolBench main experiments (Table 4): ToolLLaMA-DFSDT-Retriever achieves average Pass Rate 67.3 and Win Rate 63.1 (vs ChatGPT-ReACT reference); ToolLLaMA-DFSDT with oracle APIs gets Pass 66.7 / Win 60.0; ChatGPT-DFSDT 64.8 / 64.3; GPT-4-DFSDT highest pass among baselines (~67.0). Using the retriever's top-5 even slightly beats the oracle API set. DFSDT >> ReAct: preliminary pass rate (Table 3, ChatGPT) ReAct 35.3 -> ReACT@N 44.5 -> DFSDT 63.8 (average over I1/I2/I3). API retriever (Table 2) average NDCG@1 78.0 / NDCG@5 84.9 vs Ada 49.6/45.4 and BM25 18.5/17.0.
ablations: (1) Reasoning-strategy comparison (Table 3): DFSDT vs ReAct vs ReACT@N (cost-matched) on ChatGPT pass rate - DFSDT 63.8 avg >> ReACT@N 44.5 >> ReAct 35.3, isolating the depth-first tree-search/backtracking as the driver of improved decision-making and motivating its use for solution-path annotation. (2) Retriever comparison (Table 2): trained Sentence-BERT retriever vs BM25 vs ada-002 across I1/I2/I3 (NDCG@1/@5); the trained retriever wins everywhere; single-tool (I1) retrieval easier than multi-tool (I2/I3). (3) Retriever-vs-oracle integration (Table 4): top-5 retrieved APIs match/slightly exceed oracle-API performance, showing the retriever can substitute (and improve upon) ground-truth API specification. (4) Generalization ablation: pass/win across unseen-instruction / unseen-tool / unseen-category splits shows ToolLLaMA generalizes to unseen APIs. (5) OOD ablation: ToolLLaMA on APIBench vs Gorilla-ZS/RS (hallucination rate, AST accuracy).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval quality is reported separately (NDCG@1/@5, Table 2) from end-to-end tool-use task metrics (Pass/Win Rate via ToolEval, Table 4). DFSDT is also evaluated intrinsically (pass-rate-only preliminary study, Table 3) before being integrated into the end-to-end pipeline.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome-oriented (Pass Rate = task completion; Win Rate = solution-path quality preference, which partly reflects process/usefulness of the action sequence). Intermediate retrieval quality (NDCG) is a separate process-style metric. There is no per-step reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise accuracy metric; Win Rate's pairwise preference is the main proxy for solution-process quality.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: DFSDT trades more OpenAI API calls / compute for higher pass rate; the paper explicitly cost-matches with the ReACT@N baseline (repeat ReAct until cost equals DFSDT) and still finds DFSDT superior, indicating the gain is not merely from more compute. Retrieval narrows 16,464 APIs to top-5, drastically reducing the prompt/context and call space versus presenting all APIs. No detailed latency/token/dollar-cost tables are reported; cost is discussed qualitatively (API-call budget for pass rate; DFSDT consumes more calls than single ReAct).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed k. The API retriever feeds top-5 APIs to ToolLLaMA (k=5) in the practical setting; the oracle setting feeds the ground-truth relevant API subset. Pass rate is computed under a 'limited budget' of API calls / search steps. ~200 test instructions sampled per subset. k is fixed (5), not adaptive/precision-driven.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (not a survey; a framework + dataset + method + benchmark/evaluator paper).
benchmark_construction_and_size: ToolBench is LLM-SYNTHESIZED (auto-constructed with ChatGPT) in three stages: (i) API collection - crawl 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs across 49 categories from RapidAPI Hub (filtered for reliability); (ii) instruction generation - prompt ChatGPT to produce diverse single-tool and multi-tool instructions, using RapidAPI category/collection hierarchy (sample 2-5 tools, <=3 APIs each) to form I1/I2/I3; (iii) solution-path annotation - ChatGPT runs DFSDT to find valid API-call chains, keeping only passed paths. Answer verifiability: NOT fixed ground-truth (RapidAPI temporal variability + infinite valid paths), so evaluated reference-free via ChatGPT-based ToolEval (pass/win rate), validated at 87.1%/80.3% human agreement. Difficulty signal: even GPT-4-DFSDT and ToolLLaMA-DFSDT-Retriever reach only ~67 average pass rate, and ReAct alone ~35, showing the benchmark is far from saturated. ~200 test instances per subset; six test subsets.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023, reasoning+acting) as the reasoning-strategy predecessor extended by DFSDT; Self-Instruct / Alpaca-style automatic instruction generation with ChatGPT; AlpacaEval (Li et al. 2023) for the model-based pairwise evaluator design (ToolEval); LLaMA (Touvron et al. 2023) as the base model; Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) and BERT-BASE (Devlin et al. 2019) for the dense API retriever; BM25 and OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 as retrieval baselines; Gorilla/APIBench (Patil et al. 2023) for OOD evaluation; broader tool-learning line (Toolformer, HuggingGPT, WebGPT, etc.).
contrasts_with: ReAct / single-chain reasoning (DFSDT adds tree search + backtracking + multi-trace evaluation); closed-source tool-use LLMs (ChatGPT/GPT-4) that ToolLLaMA aims to match with an open model; Gorilla / APIBench (single-domain ML-hub APIs, retrieval-aware fine-tuning) - ToolBench covers 16k+ multi-domain RapidAPI APIs and multi-tool multi-step instructions; prior tool benchmarks with small/limited API sets, real-API instability, and missing multi-tool/multi-step scenarios.
lineage: Group E (tool use). A foundational large-scale real-world tool-use framework/benchmark: introduces ToolBench (16,464 RapidAPI APIs, 49 categories), the DFSDT decision-tree solver, a trained dense API retriever over the full pool, and the ChatGPT-based ToolEval (pass/win rate). Sits at the intersection of tool retrieval (API retriever), agentic tree-search planning (DFSDT), and instruction tuning (ToolLLaMA). Directly seeds the 'ToolBench' lineage (later StableToolBench, and many tool-retrieval works, e.g., ToolRet/ToolGen/Re-Invoke/ToolScaler benchmark against it).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). No retrieved-case adaptation step; retrieved APIs are used directly as the callable toolset and the LLM solves via DFSDT.
